envelope.text: THE BOUND: `future` is an `rclcpp::Future<Response>`, not a

why:
rclcpp returns a `std::shared_future` a caller `get()`s, and `spin_until_future_complete` drives the executor underneath. Ours returns a `Promise` the caller drives explicitly (`promise.wait(&mut executor, timeout)`) -- RFC-0021. needs a future and a runtime to await it. RFC-0021 makes every blocking helper take the executor and drive it (`promise.wait(&mut executor, timeout)`), which is what makes a timeout reliable on a single-threaded transport. The arity matches by coincidence, which is why the correlator files it `arity-only`.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-18, stated against upstream. `rclcpp::Client::async_send_request` returns a future KEYED BY THE SEQUENCE NUMBER `rcl_send_request` produced, which is what makes more than one outstanding request well-defined. Ours cannot: the sequence number is discarded at three layers and the future's slot is a hardcoded 0 — see `cpp:PollClient::send_request` for the measurement. A caller with two requests in flight gets whichever reply lands first, on both futures, with no error.

Disposition ADOPT. Nothing platform-shaped is in the way — the sequence number EXISTS at every layer and is explicitly thrown away (`_seq`) — so this is a correlation table the arena can hold, not a capability the constraints forbid. Until it exists, the honest alternative under the rule is to refuse the second concurrent request loudly rather than to serve it wrongly.

issue 1996 (2026-10-23) -- the SHAPE half landed; the correlation half above did not. On a hosted (`NROS_CPP_STD`) build `rclcpp::PollClient<S>::async_send_request(const std::shared_ptr<Request>&)` sends `*request` through `send_request` and returns the same `rclcpp::Future`, whose `get()` returns the reply as an owning `std::shared_ptr<Response>` (`cpp:Future::get`) and whose `wait_for(duration)` returns `std::future_status` while DRIVING the executor (`cpp:Future::wait_for`), with `valid()` beside them -- so the stock `minimal_client` ports with zero edited lines. What still differs and keeps this row's disposition ADOPT rather than closed: the future is not keyed by the sequence number, so two requests in flight on one client still cross-deliver, exactly as stated above; and there is no `.future` / `.request_id` / `share()` (no `std::shared_future`).

issue 2009 (2026-10-23) -- the CORRELATION half landed. Every `rclcpp::Future` a `PollClient` hands out is keyed by its request's sequence id (`nros_cpp_service_client_send_request_seq` / `_take_response_seq` carry it across the FFI, where all three layers used to drop it) and linked into the client's pending list (`rclcpp::detail::PendingList`, an intrusive list of the futures themselves: no heap, no table to size). Any number of requests may be in flight on one client; a reply reaches only the future whose id it carries, whichever future polls first; a reply for a removed, destroyed or pruned future is dropped. The bound on how many is the transport's own outstanding-request limit, past which the send is refused and the future comes back empty; a backend that cannot assign ids keeps one request in flight. Held by `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/client_seq_correlation_runtime.cpp` in `just check cpp`. What still keeps this row ADOPT rather than closed: there is no `.future` / `.request_id` / `share()` (no `std::shared_future`), and the name lives on the poll client rather than on `rclcpp::Client`.

Tracked as issue 2037 (2026-10-25): the `FutureAndRequestId` member surface (`.future`, `.request_id`) and `share()` to a `SharedFutureAndRequestId`. The future already holds its request id since issue 2009; it is not exposed.

issue 2037 (2026-10-25) -- the MEMBER SURFACE landed. On a hosted build `PollClient<S>::async_send_request(shared_ptr)` returns `PollClient<S>::FutureAndRequestId`: the future as the public member `.future` and the request's sequence id as `.request_id` (the id the reply is matched on, issue 2009; C++17 structured bindings work), with `get()` / `wait_for()` / `valid()` / `is_ready()` forwarding to the future, and `share()` returning a `SharedFutureAndRequestId` whose `future` IS-A `std::shared_future<SharedResponse>` (`rclcpp::detail::DrivenSharedFuture`, which drives the executor while it waits), so every copy gets the same response. `remove_pending_request` takes the id or either wrapper. What still keeps this row ADOPT-BOUNDED rather than closed: `.future` is an `rclcpp::Future<Response>`, not a `std::future` (nothing fulfils a promise from another thread, RFC-0021; it has the members a caller uses), the name lives on the poll client rather than on `rclcpp::Client`, the callback overload `async_send_request(request, callback)` and `SharedFutureWithRequestAndRequestId` are absent, and `share()` needs `std::promise` (refused, `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_SHARED_FUTURE`, on a freestanding build or a libstdc++ without threads). Held by `client_future_and_request_id_runtime.cpp` and `client_share_freestanding_probe.cpp` in `just check cpp`.
